| U.SPC-T396 | 2026-10-21 | feature | open | Empire decline and isolation (owner idea, Rome/Ozymandias): polities can die as well as grow. Shocks such as war, famine from broken shipping lanes (People.cs already has FaminePerDay but nothing collapses), disease/epidemics, and other disasters can decimate a system and cut it off from the gate network; the simulation keeps running for the cut-off system, which must rebuild its warp gates and fleets to rejoin. Isolation erodes loyalty: a colony or group left distant or cut off long enough drifts and can come back as a different faction entirely (secession / new polity with its own name, colours and relations). Needs design first: the shocks and their triggers, how a system is severed and reconnects, a loyalty/drift measure driven by distance and time out of contact, and when drift tips into a new faction. | owner 2026-10-21 |
| U.SPC-T397 | 2026-10-21 | chore | closed | Research spike: how real civilizations rise and fall, mapped onto the SpaceGod simulation. Study historical cases (Rome, Bronze Age collapse, Ozymandias/New Kingdom Egypt, the Mongols and their successor khanates, Byzantium, the Spanish/British empires, the Soviet breakup, the Great Schism and Reformation, the Black Death) for the drivers of rise and decline: conquest and overextension, logistical/supply failure (broken trade and shipping lanes, famine), rebellion and secession of distant provinces, religious and ideological schisms, plague, fiscal collapse/debasement, succession crises, and climate/resource shocks; plus rebound and recovery. For each driver: the mechanism, its triggers and feedback loops, its rough timescales, and how it maps onto existing Core systems (People.cs FaminePerDay, Polities, War, Contracts/trade, GateNetwork/GateConstruction, Law, Outlaws). Deliver docs/CIVILIZATION_DYNAMICS_SPIKE.md with the proposed model (state variables such as loyalty, legitimacy, cohesion, belief and supply, and the transitions), what to build first, and implementation tickets filed for each mechanic. Feeds U.SPC-T396. | docs/CIVILIZATION_DYNAMICS_SPIKE.md, commit 9de1ab1 |
| U.SPC-T398 | 2026-10-21 | feature | open | Civ dynamics: logistics collapse. When shipping lanes or gates break down (war, piracy, sabotage, lost hulls), a system that depends on imported food/goods runs short; shortages cascade into famine (extend People.cs FaminePerDay), unrest and population loss, and the shortfall spreads to systems that relied on it as a hub. Model per-system import dependence and supply stockpiles. Design from U.SPC-T397. | U.SPC-T396 |
| U.SPC-T399 | 2026-10-21 | feature | open | Civ dynamics: disease and epidemics. Outbreaks start in a system and spread along trade and passenger traffic (gates, lanes, freighters, buses); they kill or weaken population, crews and productivity, and trigger quarantines (closed ports, embargoed gates) that themselves break supply. Recovery and immunity over time. Design from U.SPC-T397. | U.SPC-T396 |
| U.SPC-T400 | 2026-10-21 | feature | open | Civ dynamics: severed systems. A system can be cut off from the gate network (gates destroyed, abandoned or unmaintained, relays lost); the simulation keeps running for it in isolation, and it must rebuild its warp gates and fleets (GateConstruction) to reconnect. Track time out of contact. Design from U.SPC-T397. | U.SPC-T396 |
| U.SPC-T401 | 2026-10-21 | feature | open | Civ dynamics: loyalty and cohesion drift. Each system/colony gets a loyalty to its polity that erodes with distance from the capital, time out of contact, neglect, heavy taxation, and misrule, and recovers with contact, investment and protection. It feeds rebellion, secession and schism. Design from U.SPC-T397. | U.SPC-T396 |
| U.SPC-T402 | 2026-10-21 | feature | open | Civ dynamics: rebellion and secession. Low-loyalty systems rise in revolt (local garrisons and fleets defect or fight), and a colony left alone long enough can come back as a different faction entirely: a new polity with its own name, colours, government and relations, possibly hostile to its old masters. Design from U.SPC-T397. | U.SPC-T396 |
| U.SPC-T403 | 2026-10-21 | feature | open | Civ dynamics: religious and ideological schisms. Give populations a belief/ideology that can drift and split; schisms divide a polity (or cross polity lines), change alliances and loyalties, spark persecution, migration and holy war, and can found new factions. Design from U.SPC-T397. | U.SPC-T396 |
| U.SPC-T404 | 2026-10-21 | feature | open | Civ dynamics: conquest and overextension. Conquest grows a polity but each held system adds administrative and garrison cost and stretches supply lines; past its reach, cohesion falls, revolts rise and defence thins, so empires can outgrow what they can hold. Design from U.SPC-T397. | U.SPC-T396 |
| U.SPC-T405 | 2026-10-21 | feature | open | Civ dynamics: fiscal crisis. A polity whose treasury fails (war costs, lost trade, debasement) cannot pay crews and garrisons: fleets desert, mutiny or turn pirate, services and gate maintenance lapse, and loyalty falls. Design from U.SPC-T397. | U.SPC-T396 |
| U.SPC-T406 | 2026-10-21 | feature | open | Civ dynamics: succession and leadership crises. A polity leadership can fall (death, coup, disputed succession), splitting it into rival claimants and civil war that pulls fleets and systems to each side, until one wins or the polity splits for good. Design from U.SPC-T397. | U.SPC-T396 |
| U.SPC-T407 | 2026-10-21 | feature | open | Civ dynamics: resource and stellar shocks. Resource depletion (mined-out belts, exhausted worlds) and natural disasters (stellar flares, impacts, habitat failures) can cripple a system economy and population and set off the other decline mechanics. Design from U.SPC-T397. | U.SPC-T396 |
| U.SPC-T408 | 2026-10-21 | feature | open | Civ dynamics: death, dark ages and recovery. A polity can die outright (all systems lost, absorbed or seceded) and leave ruins and derelicts; isolated or collapsed systems can sink into a dark age (lost tech/industry) and later recover, reconnect, and either rejoin, be reconquered, or rise as successor states. Design from U.SPC-T397. | U.SPC-T396 |
| U.SPC-T409 | 2026-10-21 | feature | open | Civ dynamics: making rise and fall visible. Surface these events to the player: galaxy map overlays for loyalty, supply, plague and severed systems, news/hails when systems revolt, starve or secede, and a history log of polities rising, splitting and dying. Design from U.SPC-T397. | U.SPC-T396 |

| U.SPC-T411 | 2026-10-21 | docs | closed | Write the owner core design principles into the repo where every agent reads them (a Design principles section in README.md, pointed to from AGENTS.md), and hold all new work to them: (1) Expandability and extensibility first: new mechanics (civ dynamics, ship types, factions, systems) plug in through clear extension points and data, not edits scattered through core loops. (2) The universe is fully flyable: given long enough, a pilot can fly from one end of the galaxy to the other in continuous space; gates and lanes are shortcuts, never the only way, because a space game where flying never gets you anywhere is not a space game. (3) Render only what is needed: at universe scale, never render full detail for things too far or small to see; LOD, impostors/icons, culling and aggregation by apparent size. (4) No loading screens: stream content in the background; the only allowed cover is visual trickery at jump gates that buys time for model loading. | bb3d23e |

| U.SPC-T470 | 2026-10-23 | feature | closed | Hardpoints on the hull, facilities inside it (owner 2026-10-23): split ship construction into two kinds of part. A hardpoint is a place on the hull's surface (gun and turret mounts, launchers, torpedo tubes, shield emitters, engine mounts) with a position and firing arc, as Construction's Hardpoint already is. A facility is a thing inside the body of the ship (Marine Habitat, Assault Bay, hangar, cargo holds, magazines, reactor, quarters, bridge and the rest) and has no arc, only a size. Every hull has a limited internal space, and each facility takes a share of it sized to what it is, so a design is a trade-off: a hull that carries a marine habitat and an assault bay gives up hold, hangar or magazine space, and a hull too small for a facility cannot fit it at all. Today internal bays are modelled as a hardpoint slot kind (SlotKind.InternalBay, Hardpoint.LayoutIndex -1, sockets named bay-N); move them out into the facility layout, and have the yard, the outfitting screen, the AI's designs and the boarding interior's compartments all read facilities from it. Builds on U.SPC-T377 | FacilitiesTests (67a318d) |
| U.SPC-T471 | 2026-10-23 | docs | closed | Ship roster and doctrine canon (owner 2026-10-23): write docs/SHIP_ROSTER.md, linked from README and docs/VISION.md, holding the owner's roster as the reference every ship ticket builds to: the three travel layers (jump gates as the strategic chokepoints, self-contained FTL on carriers, gate breakers and some capitals, hyper lanes inside a system with predictable routes that invite ambush and sabotage); every class with its role and how it travels (the own-FTL table); the strike craft; the weapons-by-tier table; the softened realism rules (inertial dampeners are why piloted dogfights work; bridges buried at the centre of the hull with no viewports, seen out through sensors and holo/VR; radiators a weak point on big ships but not a constant worry; full 3D combat, above all in dogfights; shields, so bombers knock shields down and then torpedo); and the two doctrines, a large but predictable gate fleet against a smaller jump strike group that can arrive anywhere | 6767e2f |

| U.SPC-T501 | 2026-10-23 | feature | closed | Shields come from emitters, not facing arcs (owner 2026-10-23): since everything fights in full 3D, the facing-arc shields (Facing, Broadsides.ShieldTrim and StepShields, the bow/beam/stern split from docs/SHIELD_ARCS_SPIKE.md) go away. Instead, like turrets, ships carry shield emitters as hardpoints on the hull; each emitter projects a field over the patch of hull around it, fire that lands on a patch drains that emitter's field, and a field shot away (or an emitter destroyed) leaves that spot of the hull unshielded while the rest stays covered, so a ship can be holed in one place and protected elsewhere. Emergency repair crews inside the ship (extending today's damage control teams) restore shield emitters and turrets given time. Shots hit the shield of the patch they actually strike in 3D. AI gunners and the player's aim can focus fire on a weakened patch. Every rate as a setting. Update docs (retire SHIELD_ARCS_SPIKE's arc model, SHIP_ROSTER, README) | 8c089e7 ShieldEmitterTests |

| U.SPC-T575 | 2026-10-24 | fix | closed | Law and trade-desk notices overwrite each other in the single toast slot: UnitySpaceApp.ShowLawNotices (~1202-1208) calls ShowToast twice and ShowToast replaces Toast, so a back-door sale customs catches shows only 'Customs at X seize...' and never the 'CRIME: smuggling' line, and a button's own toast is wiped at once; join both lists into one toast or queue toasts (found by bughunt) | 80d5db6 |
| U.SPC-T576 | 2026-10-24 | fix | closed | Ships running out to engage their cruise drive are labelled as bound for 'a jump gate': a cruise voyage's GateKm is the edge of the well (InterstellarTraffic.cs ~678), not a gate, yet the ship card (Hud.cs ~1918-1926, ~2047-2049) reads 'Burning toward a jump gate's approach' for the whole run out (about a week for a carrier); check Voyage.ByCruise and label it the run to the edge of the well (found by bughunt) | 9df5f36 |
| U.SPC-T577 | 2026-10-24 | fix | closed | The player's own sightings give away hidden havens: Outlaws.cs ~419 records the wanted player's sighting with (pilotBody, 'near ' + BodyName) without Hide(), so with an undiscovered haven nearby every board prints its rock and hunters fly straight to it, contrary to the doc ('the sighting names no rock'); wrap the location in Hide(...) (found by bughunt) | 9653f72 |
| U.SPC-T578 | 2026-10-24 | fix | closed | A raider captain whose flagship comes home from abroad stays 'ashore' for good: Outlaws.SettleFates (~347) sets Ashore when the hull leaves and Sync (~377) skips the returning hull because it is already in byShip, so nothing clears the flag, the captain is never sighted again, hunters drop the contract and a later Rebind strips the real flagship's record; clear Ashore in SettleFates when the ship is present, alive and still pirate (found by bughunt) | 53c2cdb |
| U.SPC-T579 | 2026-10-24 | fix | closed | A freed captain is declared dead, bounty paid or lapsed, when the prize hull they used to command is destroyed: when a flagship is taken its byShip and Law.Captains entries are never removed (Outlaws.cs ~576-583, Hold ~725, Free ~760), so after the captain is ransomed or breaks out and the prize dies under its captor's colours the outlaw is 'Killed'; drop those entries on capture or require the captain aboard there and in ClaimInBattle (found by bughunt) | df4fa6f |
| U.SPC-T580 | 2026-10-24 | fix | closed | The FTL autopilot's out-run propellant is charged up front and never refunded: FtlAutopilot.Engage (FtlNavigation.cs ~316) deducts OutRunFuelTonnes and Disengage (~414-428) refunds nothing, so a run broken a second in by a fight or hunters loses it all and re-engaging charges it again; refund the unflown share on disengage as Fleet.RefundUnflown does for AI ships (found by bughunt) | a65aa4a |
| U.SPC-T581 | 2026-10-24 | fix | closed | Selling stolen goods on a lawless station's black market creates money and earns the station a port tax: Economy.cs ~1116-1125 pays the player BlackMarket.SaleValue and credits the owner a 4% tax while debiting nothing, whereas the clans' BlackMarket.Sell debits the owner's treasury as the class doc says; debit the owner by the value and charge no port tax on black sales (found by bughunt) | a2da8e2 |
| U.SPC-T582 | 2026-10-24 | fix | closed | The Buy toast says 'cargo hold is full' for any partial purchase: Hud.cs ~2812 reports a full hold whenever fewer crates were bought than asked, even when credits or the port's stock ran out after 4 of 10; have BuyIntoHold return why it stopped and report that (found by bughunt) | 4613c8f |
| U.SPC-T583 | 2026-10-24 | fix | closed | A warehouse can be bought at a ruin and the house loses the price the next day: Holdings.BuyWarehouse (~551) has no Fallen check, so at an abandoned colony whose owner is still lawful the price goes to that owner and the next daily round writes the warehouse off as 'lost with the abandoned ...'; refuse fallen ports there and in BuyShare (found by bughunt) | 19b626c |
| U.SPC-T584 | 2026-10-24 | fix | closed | A charter pays one more day of hire than its term: Charters.cs ~263 pays hire on every daily tick and ends on the first tick at or after EndJd, so a hull taken out between ticks (the normal case) pays 31 days on a 30-day charter (the test only covers a take exactly on a tick); end before paying once jd >= EndJd or pro-rate the first and last days (found by bughunt) | 0acc1b1 |
| U.SPC-T585 | 2026-10-24 | fix | closed | A hunter whose flagship dies abroad is dropped before its heir gets home: Outlaws.PruneHunters (~1219) removes rows for hulls that are Destroyed but not GateDeparted, so OnSuccession finds nothing and the heir stops hunting, contrary to the doc ('A hunter gone through a gate keeps its row'); keep rows for hunters away on a Hunt voyage until Home resolves the succession (found by bughunt) | c721f0a |
| U.SPC-T586 | 2026-10-24 | fix | closed | Hunters away on a hunt do not count toward HunterCap: Outlaws.cs ~1139-1140 counts only hunters whose hull is in this system's fleet, so in Alpha Centauri (cap 1) sending the one hunter abroad lets the guild buy a second group and there are two when it returns; count every non-retired, undestroyed hunter still under its faction wherever it is (found by bughunt) | 33bf60a |
| U.SPC-T587 | 2026-10-25 | fix | closed | CombatTests.ABattleshipWithItsForwardBatteryKnockedOutTurnsBroadsideInstead is flaky: it failed in two combined filter runs (Broadside+Combat+WeakPatch+FireCone/Fighter) after U.SPC-T557's turn-inertia change, the battleship still bow-on (0.2 deg) when a broadside was expected, yet it passes alone and with its own class; find the shared state or ordering/seed dependency between fixtures (or a turn that now needs longer to come round) and make the test deterministic (found by bughunt follow-up) | b4ba0cf |
| U.SPC-T588 | 2026-10-25 | fix | closed | A bounty hunter group wiped out abroad leaves its row Away forever: U.SPC-T585 made Outlaws.PruneHunters skip rows with BountyHunter.Away so an heir can come home and inherit, but when the whole hunt group dies abroad nobody comes home and the row is never pruned, so Outlaws.Hunters grows; clear Away wherever a Hunt voyage ends with no survivor (found by U.SPC-T585 review) | ABountyHunterGroupWipedOutAbroadHasItsRowPruned |
